prompt_source: Ch9 three-email sequence brief (lines 1644-1652), with Ch7 sample kit plus <offer>/<proof>

turns.prompt:
<bio>
Maya Torres is a career coach for mid-career nurses who want to move
into healthcare leadership without leaving patient care behind. After
14 years as an ICU nurse and four as a nurse manager, she started her
practice in 2023. She is known for practical, no-nonsense sessions and
a habit of asking "What would you tell a new grad in your shoes?"
</bio>

<audience>
Registered nurses, 8 to 20 years in, mostly women in their late 30s to
40s. Respected on their units, often the informal charge nurse, but
passed over or unsure about formal leadership. Fear: becoming "a
suit" who forgets the floor. Desire: influence over how care is
delivered. Phrases they use (from client intake forms): "I'm already
doing the job, just without the title." "I don't want to sell out."
Inference, unconfirmed: many are the main earner in their household.
</audience>

<message>
You do not have to choose between leading and caring. The best nurse
leaders lead because they care, and the skills that make you good at
the bedside are most of what leadership needs.
</message>

<voice>
1. Short sentences. 2. Starts with a scene from a shift. 3. Uses
nursing language naturally, never explains it. 4. Warm but blunt.
5. No exclamation marks. 6. One question to the reader per piece,
near the end. 7. Never uses "self-care" or "empower." 8. Humor is
dry and about hospital life. 9. Ends with a concrete next step.
10. Signs off "Maya."
</voice>

<offer>
Charge to Chair: a six-week online leadership program for RNs with 8+ years of experience. Six live Tuesday-evening Zoom sessions (7 to 8:30 p.m. Pacific), weekly worksheets, and one 30-minute 1:1 call with Maya. Price $690, or 3 payments of $240. Cohort limited to 20 seats so every 1:1 call fits in Maya's calendar. Starts November 17, 2026.
</offer>

<proof>
"I went from informal charge nurse to unit educator in four months, and I still work two bedside shifts a month." Dana R., RN, ICU, pilot cohort 2025 (shared with permission).
</proof>

Write a three-email sequence for the program in <offer>, using my kit.
Email 1 (problem aware): the "already doing the job" frustration; no
pitch; ends with a question to reply to.
Email 2: why generic leadership training does not fit nurses; introduce
the program; one real testimonial from <proof>.
Email 3: the offer, the real enrollment deadline of November 10, 2026, and the
three most common objections answered.
Each under 250 words. Subject line plus preview text for each. Use
only facts in <offer> and <proof>. Write [NEED] where proof is missing.
turns.output:
**Email 1**
Subject: Already charge. Still not listed.
Preview: The job is yours. The title is not.

The assignment board is wrong again. You fix it before huddle. You hand the new grad the hard room. You catch the potassium before it hits the chart. Nobody asked. You just did it.

Then the manager posts the leadership role. Your name is not on the short list. The person who got it asks you how the unit actually runs.

You have done this for years. Informal charge. Preceptor. The one who stays for report so the next shift does not walk in blind. The job is yours. The title is not.

That gap is not a personality flaw. It is a missing translation. Bedside skill does not read as leadership on a requisition. You know that. It still stings when you clock out and someone else is "the leader."

You do not have to become someone else to be seen. The read of a room that keeps a patient safe is what a unit needs from the person in the chair.

Hit reply with two sentences. What would you tell a new grad in your shoes, the one already running the shift with no title?

Maya.

**Email 2**
Subject: The binder stayed in the locker
Preview: Generic leadership class does not survive a short-staffed Tuesday.

You sat through the hospital leadership day. Slides. A binder. Trust-fall energy you did not sign up for. Then the rapid response pager went off. You went back to the unit. The binder stayed in the locker.

Generic leadership training is built for people who left the work. You have not. You still take a patient. You still know who is drowning at 03:00. A framework that dies on a short-staffed Tuesday is not a framework. It is a conference.

You do not need a new personality. You need the bedside read turned into language a director will fund. You need a chair you can sit in without dropping the floor.

That is Charge to Chair. Six weeks. Online. For RNs with 8 or more years in. Six live sessions. The point is the job you already do, not a costume.

Dana R., RN, ICU, pilot cohort 2025, shared this with permission. "I went from informal charge nurse to unit educator in four months, and I still work two bedside shifts a month."

You do not have to choose between leading and caring. The skills that make you good at the bedside are most of what leadership needs.

What did the last leadership class get wrong about your unit?

Reply with that one thing. I read them.

Maya.

**Email 3**
Subject: November 10 is the close
Preview: Twenty seats. Six Tuesdays. $690 or three payments.

The charge sheet has your handwriting on it again. You are in the med room, moving the new grad off that patient. The role posts. You talk yourself out of it between med passes.

Charge to Chair starts November 17, 2026. Enrollment closes November 10, 2026. Six weeks, online, for RNs with 8 or more years in. Six live Zoom sessions, Tuesdays, 7 to 8:30 p.m. Pacific. Weekly worksheets. One 30-minute 1:1 with me. $690, or three payments of $240. Twenty seats. The cap exists so every 1:1 fits on my calendar.

Three objections. A ranked tally is [NEED].

"I don't want to sell out." Then don't. Leading and caring are not a trade. Dana R., RN, ICU, pilot cohort 2025, shared with permission: "I went from informal charge nurse to unit educator in four months, and I still work two bedside shifts a month." One nurse. [NEED] for anyone else's result.

"I'm already doing the job, just without the title." Then the work is the title, not a new personality. [NEED] for a syllabus.

Time and cost. Six Tuesday evenings, worksheets, one call. $690, or three payments of $240. [NEED] for refund terms, and for how a 7 p.m. Pacific start lands after nights.

Which of those is yours?

Reply "seat" before November 10. I will send the link.

Maya.
